Turner syndrome is a chromosomal condition that affects development in females. It is caused by a type of aneuploidy known as monosomy, specifically monosomy of the X chromosome.

A normal human karyotype (the complete set of chromosomes) consists of 46 chromosomes: 22 pairs of autosomes and 1 pair of sex chromosomes (XX for females, XY for males).

In Turner syndrome, an individual is missing one of the two sex chromosomes. This means they have only one X chromosome instead of the usual two (XX).

This results in a total of 45 chromosomes in each cell.

The chromosomal composition is written as 45, XO, where the 'O' signifies the absence of the second sex chromosome.

Further Insights:

Common characteristics of the syndrome include short stature, a webbed neck, and non-functioning ovaries, which can lead to infertility.

The condition is not inherited from an affected parent; it occurs as a random event during the formation of reproductive cells (eggs or sperm).

A convex lens is a converging lens, and the type of image it forms is entirely dependent on the distance of the object from the optical center of the lens.

Case 1: Object is placed beyond the focal point (F).

When the object is placed at a distance greater than the focal length (e.g., at 2F, or between F and 2F, or beyond 2F), the convex lens converges the light rays to form a real and inverted image on the opposite side of the lens. This image can be projected onto a screen.

Case 2: Object is placed between the focal point (F) and the optical center.

When the object is placed within the focal length of the lens, the rays of light diverge after passing through the lens. They appear to come from a point on the same side of the lens as the object. This creates a virtual, erect, and magnified image. This is the principle behind a simple magnifying glass.

Let's analyze why the other options are incorrect:

A convex lens always forms real and inverted images only. This is incorrect. As explained in Case 2, it can also form a virtual and erect image.

A convex lens always forms virtual images only. This is incorrect. As explained in Case 1, it most often forms real and inverted images.

A convex lens cannot magnify objects. This is incorrect. A convex lens is the basis of a magnifying glass. It produces a magnified image when the object is placed within its focal length, and it can also produce magnified real images (when the object is placed between F and 2F).

Further Insights:

The ability of a convex lens to form both real and virtual images makes it incredibly versatile.

It is used in cameras, projectors, and the human eye to form real images.

It is used in magnifying glasses, microscopes, and telescopes (as the eyepiece) to form virtual images.

The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Simple Present Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Simple Past Tense.

"That" is used in place of Inverted Commas while transforming the sentence from Direct Speech to Indirect Speech.

For example:

He said, "I never go to the village." (Direct Speech)

He said that he never went to the village. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· The reporting verb 'said to' is changed into 'told'.

· The pronoun 'I' is changed into 'he'.

· The verb 'do' (simple present) is changed into 'did' (simple past).

· The possessive determiner 'your' is changed into 'my'.

· 'Right now' is changed into 'right then'.

For example:

questions.solution:
The given sentence is in a comparative degree, indicating that the new knife is "much sharper" than something else, and it "cuts effortlessly." We are required to express this sentence in a positive degree of comparison. A positive degree simply describes a quality or characteristic without making any comparisons.

Option (a) - This option maintains the comparative degree ("sharper") and doesn't express the sentence in the positive degree.

Option (b)- This option shows a superlative degree ("the sharpest") and doesn't rephrase the sentence in the positive degree.

Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

Note:

· The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

Note:

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

2) We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

questions.question: In the question given below, a sentence is given with one part bracketed. Select the option that provides the correct replacement for the bracketed part. questions.questionHtml:

questions.solution:
The original phrase "(cut of)" is grammatically incorrect. "Cut of" is not a standard phrasal verb in English.

The phrasal verb "cut short" means to end something earlier than planned or to interrupt something.

In the context of the sentence, the speech was interrupted and ended abruptly because of Jack's actions. Therefore, "cut short" is the most appropriate replacement.

(b): cut out: This means to remove something or to stop doing something. It doesn't fit the context of interrupting a speech.

(c): cut up: This can mean to cut something into pieces or to be very upset. Neither meaning works here.

The corrected sentence would read: "The end of this speech was suddenly cut short by Jack tripping up Roger's heels and tumbling him into a mass of thick shrubs."

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Rearrange the steps of building a simple sandcastle tower in the correct order: P. Flip the filled bucket upside down onto a flat patch of sand. Q. questions.questionHtml:

Q. Decorate the finished sand tower with shells and seaweed.

R. Fill a bucket completely with damp, packed sand.

S. Carefully lift the bucket straight up to reveal the molded sand tower.
questions.solution:

(S): Then, the mold must be removed to reveal the structure. This can only happen after it has been flipped.

They do not change their form (spelling) and they have no infinitive or participle (past/present). Example: I can speak Spanish. questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb ['be'] and the preposition "by" is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The sentence in the Active voice should be in the Infinitive form (to + V1 form).

The format in Passive voice is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + have/has/had + to + be + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format in the Active voice is: Subject + have/has/had + to + V1 + Object.

For example:

Some books had to be lent by me. (Passive)

I had to lend some books. (Active)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (c): The city council had to demolish the old building because it was deemed unsafe for public occupation.

questions.solution:
The blank requires a relative pronoun to relate the subject 'the person' and 'the car'. Among the options, (a) denotes the location of a place and so it is negated. Filling the blank with whom answers the following question: To whom does the car belong? That person must be a wealthy person.

Relative pronouns: A relative pronoun is used to connect a clause or phrase to a noun or pronoun. The clause modifies, or describes, the noun. The most common relative pronouns are who, whom, whose, which, and that. For example: She is the girl who received the award for bravery from our Home Minister.

The usage of a "to be" form ['were'] of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

The sentence contains an infinitive ("to submit"). The format in Active voice is: Subject + V2 + Object + to + V1.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case) + to + V1.

She told me to leave. (Active)

questions.solution:
·In a sentence like this, when 'If' is used, it always agrees with the past perfect tense (when "would have" is there).

·The incident that happens first or was supposed to happen first takes a past perfect tense. In this sentence, the person should have "studied" before, and thus, "had" is placed before "studied".

·For example: I would've passed if I had studied.

·The three types of conditional sentences (with examples) are given in the table.

IIf I study (V1)I will pass the exam
IIIf I studied (V2)I would pass the exam
IIIIf I had studied (had + V3)I would have passed the exam

·The question agrees with the third conditional given in the table above.

·Thus, "I had studied" should replace "I studied".

·Therefore, the correct answer is:(a) I had studied.

·The corrected form of the sentence is: If I had studied, I would have aced the new departmental exam.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate tense form to fill in the blank. The students _____ for the final exam.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate tense form to fill in the blank.

The students _____ for the final exam.
questions.solution:
The subject "the students" is plural. Thus, the verb must agree with the plural subject. "Were" is the past tense of "be" used with plural subjects. "Preparing" is the present participle form of the verb "prepare." Together, "were preparing" forms the past continuous tense, which indicates an ongoing action in the past. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

The final sentence: The students were preparing for the final exam.

(b) - "Was" is the past tense of "be" used with singular subjects.

(c)- "Had" is used in the past perfect tense but should be followed by the past participle (not the present participle (-ing form)). The correct form for past perfect would be "had prepared," not "had preparing."

(d)- "Was" is singular, and "prepared" is the past participle form. Together, "was prepared" implies a passive voice, which is not appropriate here.

Note:

· The past participle is a form of a verb that typically ends in "-ed," "-en," or other irregular endings in English. It is used in various verb constructions, including perfect tenses, passive voice, and adjectives.

· Subject-verb agreement refers to the grammatical principle that a verb must agree in number with its subject.

· Active voice: She bought a new car. (She is the subject and a new car is an object.) Passive voice: A new car was bought by her. (A new car is a subject and her is the object.)

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence. Part (O) "to renewable energy sources" is a prepositional phrase that completes the subject, specifying what kind of transition it is: "The global transition to renewable energy sources." So far: "The global transition to renewable energy sources".

Part (P) "is essential for combating climate change" provides the predicate for the subject. "is essential" is the verb phrase, and "for combating climate change" explains the first reason for its essential nature.

Part (Q) "and building a sustainable future" adds a second, parallel reason connected by "and," further explaining why the transition is essential.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Unwanted expenses have incur this month.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

Unwanted expenses have incur this month.
questions.solution:
The verb 'have' in the underlined phrase is to be followed by a verb in the past participle form (V3) but the verb 'incur' is in the base form. Also, a 'to-be' form of verb is required as the sentence is in Passive voice. Among the options, 'have been incurred' in option (d) is the best replacement for the underlined phrase both contextually and grammatically. 'Has been incurred' may lead to subject-verb agreement error (singular verb "has" cannot be used for plural noun "expenses"), if used as the replacement and 'have incurred' is incorrect form of verb for a Passive voice sentence. So, these two options cannot be used and thus negated.

The correct sentence is: Unwanted expenses have been incurred this month.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

Note:

Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - She likes cooking. [singular subject and verb] -- They like to cook vegetables. [plural subject and verb]

The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Present Perfect Tense or Past Simple Tense.

Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 +Object) will be converted into Present Perfect (Subject + has/have + V3 +Object).

For example:

He said that he had got a new job. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I have got a new job." (Direct Speech)

OR

Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object) will be converted into Past Simple (Subject + V2 + Object).

For example:

He said that Arya had sent him a book. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "Arya sent me a book" (Direct Speech)

The second case is applicable here [Past simple]

•The third person pronoun 'she' is changed into first person pronoun 'I'.

•The past perfect verb 'had finished' is changed into 'finished' [simple past].

Options (a) and (c) are eliminated because the statement is in passive voice while the given statement in the question is in active voice. Option (d) is eliminated because the meaning of the given statement has been changed. Option (b) is the correct answer.

The public awareness program

B. Aims to underscore

C. Exercise for maintaining

D. The importance of regular

questions.solution:
The correct order to form a meaningful sentence is BDCE. The fixed part of the sentence introduces the subject (Public awareness program). Part B follows the fixed part because it explains the purpose or goal of the program. It indicates that the program aims to highlight something. Part D then specifies the specific aspect that the program is emphasising/highlighting, which is the regularity of something. Accordingly, BD forms a necessary pair. Part C further specifies what the regularity is related to. It specifies that the program aims to highlight the importance of regular exercise. Part E completes the message of the program, specifying what the aim of regular exercise is (maintaining a healthy lifestyle). Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The complete sentence is: The public awareness program aims to underscore the importance of regular exercise for maintaining a healthy lifestyle.

The usage of a "to be" form of the verb ['is' here] is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + V1/V5 + Object.

The error in this sentence is a subject-verb agreement mistake. The subject is "the committee members," which is plural, but the verb "hasn't" (a contraction of "has not") is singular.
